metadata.title: Isekai Fantasy Character Archetypes
metadata.purpose: Research-grounded original parody casting and character design.
metadata.scope: Purposive anime-centered reference corpus, not a popularity ranking, census, or estimate of real-world trope frequencies.
metadata.spoiler_scope: Premises, introductory character identities, and basic recurring relationships; no intentional late-story plot reveal.

primary_roles.main: Viewpoint or central agency that organizes the story, irrespective of body or species.
primary_roles.party: Recurring companion, co-lead, retainer, housemate, colleague, or familiar with ongoing dramatic agency.
primary_roles.world: Local service provider, recurring institutional figure, foil, antagonist, or quest contact outside the active core cast.

recurrence_labels.broad_pattern: Editorial synthesis recurring in the reference corpus; not a measured frequency.
recurrence_labels.recognizable_subtype: A distinct useful branch, sometimes supported by a small number of anchors.
recurrence_labels.signature_exception: Especially associated with a memorable unusual example; use to change the premise.
recurrence_labels.generic_fantasy: Useful background fantasy composite; no claim of an independently established isekai-specific recurring type.

classification.premise_cost_definition: Advisory salience score 0 conventional, 1 noticeable variation, 2 premise-defining exception. Do not sum it as an empirical rarity score. Compatibility uses declared mechanism tags and cast scope.
classification.canon_vs_design: Names and narrow source connections are research anchors. Look, variants, gags, additional abilities, age defaults, and combination rules are original design proposals. Defaults must never overwrite a named source character.

archetypes.title: The ordinary looking cheat hero
archetypes.core: An apparently unremarkable newcomer solves impossible problems with an absurdly generous starting ability and becomes the center of every local crisis.
archetypes.look: Straight black or dark-brown hair, average height and lean build, plain face, and dark practical clothing. Choose a school jacket, travel coat, or simple tunic. Add one conspicuously ordinary object, such as a phone, contrasting with an increasingly prestigious sword.
archetypes.engine: Polite, helpful, and astonishingly casual about his power. He expects an uneventful life while every reasonable action becomes a public miracle. The recurring joke is the gap between his mild reaction and everyone elses dramatic interpretation.
archetypes.kit: One versatile cheat covers combat or convenient problem-solving. Require local expertise, emotional judgment, or social permission that the cheat cannot provide. Companions must retain tasks he cannot complete simply by increasing magical output.
variants: Earnest summoned student who keeps apologizing
Exhausted adult office worker seeking a quiet life

archetypes.title: The snarky opportunist adventurer
archetypes.core: A penny-pinching survivor keeps an impressive but dysfunctional team moving through schemes, complaints, and occasional flashes of genuine loyalty.
archetypes.look: Messy brown or black hair, medium height, an ordinary lean build, and visibly affordable equipment. Use a short cape, mismatched boots, a battered sword, and a tightly guarded coin purse. His posture alternates between slouching resignation and frantic bargaining.
archetypes.engine: He sees every heroic quest as a bad contract and every reward as potential rent money. He criticizes his companions relentlessly, then spends his last resources rescuing them. Let petty selfishness collide with grudging responsibility.
archetypes.kit: A bag of weak but flexible skills, favorable luck, and opportunistic planning beats individually stronger enemies. Plans require timing and cooperation; pride, greed, and unreliable partners regularly destroy the carefully calculated advantage.
variants: Lazy realist with unexpectedly good tactical instincts
Shameless negotiator who becomes the party accountant

anchors.connection: Lucky beginner adventurer and exasperated schemer.

archetypes.title: The looping suffering survivor
archetypes.core: A physically ordinary outsider acquires essential knowledge through painful repeated failures, then must persuade stronger people to act on it.
archetypes.look: Short dark hair, average build, and contemporary clothing that remains visibly foreign: tracksuit, hoodie, or convenience-store jacket. Use tired eyes, a clenched expression, and a notebook of crossed-out plans. Distinguish remembered scars from injuries the reset actually preserves.
archetypes.engine: He performs confidence because explaining the full situation is difficult or impossible. Private terror clashes with public bravado. Comedy can come from knowing trivial repetitions perfectly while still failing at ordinary conversations that matter emotionally.
archetypes.kit: A reset or retry grants information, not automatic victory. Fix the trigger, checkpoint behavior, memory rules, and cost. Other characters have independent motives; remembered facts do not guarantee their trust or obedience.
variants: Openly anxious planner who tells selected allies
Boastful optimist whose smile hides accumulated exhaustion

archetypes.title: The rejected defensive hero
archetypes.core: A publicly rejected hero turns distrust into formidable protection and gradually rebuilds a dependable team of overlooked or mistreated people.
archetypes.look: Black or deep-brown hair, guarded eyes, sturdy rather than delicate build, and a heavy cloak over practical armor. A shield should dominate his silhouette. Weathering, repairs, and a merchant satchel communicate someone who learned to survive without royal support.
archetypes.engine: He treats kindness as a possible scam and insists that every favor is a transaction. His actions repeatedly betray his protective instincts. The recurring contrast is a harsh verbal invoice attached to conspicuously generous behavior.
archetypes.kit: Exceptional defense, barriers, resistance, or protection grants allies freedom to attack. Make direct offense genuinely limited, and allow reputation to block access to resources. A trusted damage dealer therefore has a functional relationship with him.
variants: Gruff shield bearer rebuilding a good name
Disgraced support specialist with a rescue habit

archetypes.title: The betrayed gun crafting survivor
archetypes.core: A discarded weakling survives an extreme ordeal and returns as a heavily armed, abrasive problem-solver who wants control over his future.
archetypes.look: White or silver hair can mark the transformation; black remains an alternative. Use a lean muscular build, dark coat, reinforced boots, and one altered limb or conspicuous scar. A large handmade firearm contrasts sharply with the settings swords and staffs.
archetypes.engine: He claims that helping strangers is inefficient while collecting dependents faster than spare ammunition. His intimidating presentation clashes with mundane logistics: repairs, shopping, childcare, and companions who ignore his carefully rehearsed declarations of independence.
archetypes.kit: Crafting or transmutation converts knowledge into powerful equipment and improvised solutions. Limit ammunition, materials, heat, maintenance, or safe deployment. Modern-looking weapons should be a deliberate technology intrusion with consequences for the setting.

archetypes.title: The reincarnated child magic prodigy
archetypes.core: A person with memories of an earlier life starts over as a child and learns magic far earlier than anyone expects.
archetypes.look: Begin with a genuinely small child silhouette and age it consistently over the story. Hair may be brown, blond, silver, or black because the new body belongs to the fantasy world. Use oversized training robes, a beginner staff, and adultlike concentration.
archetypes.engine: Private adult commentary collides with a body that needs naps, parental permission, and appropriately sized furniture. Expertise in one life does not guarantee emotional maturity in the next. The funniest reversals let adults correctly overrule the supposed genius.
archetypes.kit: Early training and retained learning methods create unusual magical growth. Keep physical development, social status, stamina, and incomplete knowledge meaningful. The protagonist needs teachers and guardians rather than beginning with every adult competence intact.

archetypes.title: The guild strategist with glasses
archetypes.core: A socially awkward planner becomes indispensable by coordinating people, resources, and institutions more effectively than any single heroic fighter could.
archetypes.look: Dark hair, slim or average build, glasses, layered robes, and a tidy but overburdened appearance. Give the character maps, a ledger, contracts, or a casting focus. The glasses adjustment is an occasional punctuation mark, not his entire personality.
archetypes.engine: He understands battlefield coordination better than a friendly invitation. Allies interpret his pauses as sinister calculation while he is simply exhausted or embarrassed. A recurring joke lets his allegedly flawless plan depend on ordinary people behaving unpredictably.
archetypes.kit: Support magic, information, planning, negotiation, or institutional authority multiplies the groups effectiveness. Keep solo combat limited and intelligence incomplete. Competent lieutenants should occasionally improve the plan instead of functioning as pieces moved by a flawless mastermind.

archetypes.title: The theatrical secret mastermind
archetypes.core: An overwhelmingly capable fantasist pretends to be ordinary while staging dramatic secret interventions that other people interpret far more seriously.
archetypes.look: Use deliberately dull black hair, average student clothing, and modest posture in public. The secret identity has a tall hooded silhouette, flowing dark coat, gloves, and a dramatic weapon. The contrast in staging matters more than adding many accessories.
archetypes.engine: He judges life by whether a scene looks sufficiently impressive. His followers convert theatrical improvisation into a serious operation. Repeated comedy comes from elaborate presentation serving a trivial personal goal while accidentally resolving a real conspiracy.
archetypes.kit: High magical and martial ability makes the performance possible. Limit awareness, priorities, and coordination rather than inventing weak combat statistics. Followers must handle administration and consequences that he fails to notice or misunderstands.

archetypes.title: The obsessively cautious overpowered hero
archetypes.core: A hero with overwhelming potential refuses to act until every possible risk has been anticipated, rehearsed, insured against, and preferably eliminated.
archetypes.look: Dark hair, stern face, athletic adult build, and immaculate practical armor. His sword is unremarkable beside the absurd quantity of backup equipment: spare swords, labeled potions, protective charms, and a pack containing another smaller emergency pack.
archetypes.engine: He applies catastrophic worst-case thinking to harmless errands. Impatient companions demand action while his preparations consume the reward. Let some precautions prove useful so that the joke concerns excess and social cost, not caution being inherently foolish.
archetypes.kit: Exceptional training, redundancy, preparation, and overwhelming force make victories reliable. Time, money, trust, and opportunities are the price. An enemy can exploit delay or force a decision before sufficient information becomes available.
variants: Deadpan minimalist who secretly carries thirty contingencies
Polite safety obsessive who writes risk assessments for lunch

archetypes.title: The friendly monster nation builder
archetypes.core: A harmless-looking reincarnated monster acquires extraordinary capabilities and gathers isolated peoples into a growing community that soon requires actual government.
archetypes.look: Begin with a simple rounded nonhuman silhouette, such as a translucent blob, small ooze, or compact magical creature. If a humanoid form exists, give it a consistent shared color motif. A coat, scarf, or civic badge can signal leadership without erasing the monster identity.
archetypes.engine: The protagonist proposes a modest convenience and accidentally triggers geopolitical change. Friendly conversational habits survive alongside alarming power. Let the recurring joke shift from collecting abilities to discovering that every rescued group creates another public-service responsibility.
archetypes.kit: Absorption, adaptation, naming, crafting, or unusual perception gives growth and broad utility. Define one acquisition rule and its costs. Governance, conflicting needs, and resources remain collective problems that personal magical strength cannot fully solve.

archetypes.title: The undead overlord with ordinary worries
archetypes.core: A player becomes the terrifying ruler represented by an inhuman avatar and must maintain authority over followers who assume limitless wisdom.
archetypes.look: A tall skeletal body, empty face or glowing eye sockets, and broad ceremonial robes create a dominant silhouette. Use restrained black, ivory, and one jewel color. A staff, seal, or throne expresses authority; one mundane office object supplies the comic contrast.
archetypes.engine: His interior voice worries about etiquette, expenses, and disappointing old friends while his exterior cannot look reassuring. Subordinates interpret hesitation as profound strategy. Their enthusiasm magnifies small decisions into terrifying policies he may struggle to reverse.
archetypes.kit: High-level magic and a powerful organization establish overwhelming force. Limit knowledge, emotional communication, and confidence in unfamiliar rules. Retainers possess their own interpretations and methods, so issuing orders can create problems rather than instantly resolve them.

archetypes.title: The talkative spider survivalist
archetypes.core: A reincarnated person begins as vulnerable dungeon prey and survives through frantic experimentation, incremental evolution, and an almost continuous internal monologue.
archetypes.look: Keep the primary body recognizably arachnid: compact abdomen, multiple eyes, and clear leg silhouettes. Pale, dark, or jewel-colored markings can provide expression. A humanlike face is optional; exaggerated posture, thought balloons, and web patterns can carry personality without changing species.
archetypes.engine: The internal narrator is excitable, sarcastic, and easily distracted while the external creature appears frightening or incomprehensible. Every discovery becomes a tiny victory. The recurring gag contrasts triumphant self-commentary with the undignified physical reality of survival.
archetypes.kit: Webs, venom, climbing, traps, and carefully earned upgrades reward problem-solving. Preserve hunger, terrain, predator threats, and weaknesses between evolutions. A solo-survival opening can later admit allies, but a full harem is not the default structure.

archetypes.title: The sentient weapon guardian
archetypes.core: A person reincarnated as a weapon gains agency through a wielder, creating a linked adventure built around protection, teaching, and mutual dependence.
archetypes.look: Use one unmistakable weapon silhouette with a simple facial motif, central gem, or expressive ornament. Scale it clearly against its wielder. Steel, bronze, or dark iron palettes work; decorative glow should reinforce the personality rather than conceal the object shape.
archetypes.engine: The weapon delivers worried parental advice while its wielder wants to test the next dangerous technique. It may sound worldly yet lack hands for basic tasks. The relationship gains warmth when each protects the others dignity as well as safety.
archetypes.kit: Magical senses, telepathy, stored skills, or self-propulsion can grant action, but define their range and cost. Keep a meaningful reason to need a wielder. Count the pair as linked characters while preserving the weapons protagonist status.

archetypes.title: The reincarnated vending machine
archetypes.core: A modern commercial object becomes an adventuring protagonist by making its rigid product system useful in a world that has never seen it.
archetypes.look: An upright rectangular machine with product windows, buttons, coin slot, and a clearly readable dispensing hatch creates instant recognition. Use one bright commercial color and a simple light pattern for expression. Show its bulk honestly when companions transport it.
archetypes.engine: An articulate internal personality is trapped behind a tiny menu of prerecorded phrases. Ordinary customer-service language acquires ridiculous significance during danger. Companions learn the communication system, and practical generosity gradually changes a suspicious towns view of the machine.
archetypes.kit: Food, drinks, useful products, and permitted machine transformations solve specific problems. Retain movement, communication, inventory, and transaction constraints. The carrier or interpreter supplies essential agency; the object must still make decisions rather than become mere equipment.

archetypes.look: Design recipe: tall, muscular or full-built; purple, red, or indigo hair, a prominent horn, and an enormous sword. A suit, fitted uniform, or formal kimono over a powerful frame creates the secretary-and-enforcer contradiction. Give her an immaculate clipboard.
archetypes.engine: Proud, eager to help, and easily competitive. Wants to be the indispensable right hand. She treats filing, hospitality, or cooking as a battle and celebrates victory before anyone has tasted the result.
archetypes.kit: Close combat and physical protection; administration or cooking may be the comic weak point. Choose the weakness explicitly, because it is not universal to ogres. Signature object: sword plus clipboard.
variants: Formal secretary with destructive enthusiasm.
Mild-mannered male clerk who becomes an ogre-sized shield in danger.

anchors.connection: Purple-haired, horned ogre-associated combatant anchors the visual family.

archetypes.title: Proud dragon shapeshifter
archetypes.core: Ancient draconic dignity compressed into a houseguest who is surprisingly easy to annoy.
archetypes.look: Design recipe: adult human form with horns, slit-pupil eyes, one scale motif, and red, black, or white hair. Tall athletic or stately build; formal dress, armored coat, or kimono. Repeat horn shape and jewelry in the enormous dragon form.
archetypes.engine: Proud, competitive, and emotionally direct. Wants recognition as a superior being but also companionship. The running joke contrasts threats to level mountains with petty concern over rooms, snacks, or another dragon's manners.
archetypes.kit: Transformation, flight, breath attacks, or strong magic. Space, collateral damage, and social consequences keep the large form from solving every scene. Signature object: an ancient ornament treated as a mundane household item.
variants: Black-haired formal guardian.
Red-haired competitive dragon who takes every chore as a contest.

anchors.connection: A dragon-associated transforming companion.

archetypes.title: Gothic immortal vampire
archetypes.core: Stillness, lace, and an impossible age signal danger beneath a delicate appearance.
archetypes.look: Design recipe: pale palette, crimson accents, blonde, silver, or black hair; petite or tall adult silhouette. Gothic dress or severe formal coat, antique jewelry, parasol, and an unnervingly neat posture. A child-shaped version is a nonromantic supernatural role.
archetypes.engine: Cool, possessive, or ceremonious, with a stubborn private attachment. Wants trust or a secure place after isolation. She makes an ominous declaration, then reveals that its subject was seating arrangements or a stolen dessert.
archetypes.kit: Regeneration, blood-associated magic, or overwhelming spell power. Pick a setting-specific cost; do not assume every vampire has the same sunlight rule. Favorite object: old brooch, parasol, or carefully chosen teacup.
variants: Clearly adult tall aristocratic spellcaster.
Small ancient nonromantic guardian who speaks with severe formality.

archetypes.title: Demon princess with a casual manner
archetypes.core: Royal or demonic status collides with sociable curiosity and a taste for straightforward action.
archetypes.look: Design recipe: red, pink, purple, or black hair, small horns or pointed ears, and a confident adult silhouette. Practical travel clothes retain one expensive royal detail. Choose a fist-fighter stance or staff instead of automatically assigning a seductive costume.
archetypes.engine: Outgoing, adventurous, and less ceremonious than her title suggests. Wants to explore and choose her own life. She refers to catastrophic demon customs as ordinary childhood activities and cannot understand why the humans look worried.

Soft-spoken demon noble with unexpectedly blunt practical advice.

archetypes.title: Disastrously high-maintenance goddess healer
archetypes.core: A genuine source of miracles who generates almost as many emergencies as she cures.
archetypes.look: Design recipe: blue, blonde, or pale aqua hair; elegant medium-height adult form. White-and-blue ceremonial clothes, a large ribbon or halo-like ornament, impractical luggage, and a holy staff. A wine cup or embarrassing shopping receipt adds a second recognizable prop.

archetypes.kit: Healing, purification, or resurrection according to the chosen world. Low judgment, spending, or rigid divine rules limit her; she should still be useful. Favorite object: cup, offering basket, or party-trick kit.
variants: Boastful blue-haired miracle worker.
Anxious blonde rookie goddess who cannot control the hero she summoned.

archetypes.title: Earnest priestess or support mage
archetypes.core: The gentle support specialist who notices pain, logistics, and feelings the hero overlooks.
archetypes.look: Design recipe: medium or short height; white, blonde, brown, or soft pink hair, braid or simple bob. White robes with one accent color, practical boots, satchel of supplies, and a modest staff or prayer book. Slim, soft, or sturdy builds all work.
archetypes.engine: Kind, disciplined, and quietly firm. Wants everyone to come home alive. Her refusal to heal preventable stupidity for free, or insistence on rest, turns softness into authority and stops her becoming a silent admirer.
archetypes.kit: Healing, barriers, buffs, and triage; limited mana or preparation protects stakes. Give her one nonhealing skill, such as negotiation or herbcraft. Signature object: annotated prayer book or medicine pouch.
variants: Shy healer who becomes terrifying when patients ignore instructions.
Practical male cleric with the same care-and-boundaries role.

archetypes.title: Ancient small librarian
archetypes.core: The small, severe custodian of magic who appears to have been disappointed by visitors for centuries.
archetypes.look: Design recipe: small child-shaped or explicitly mature petite form; blonde ringlets, silver bob, or very long dark hair. Elaborate old-fashioned clothes, layered sleeves, large book, and a key ring. A library chair can emphasize tiny scale without sexual cues.
archetypes.engine: Aloof, fussy, lonely, and fiercely attached once trust is earned. Wants a meaningful bond while denying that need. She interrupts a dramatic crisis to enforce borrowing rules, then quietly risks herself for the group.
archetypes.kit: Deep magical knowledge, barriers, or spatial tricks with a contract or location condition. Knowledge need not equal social wisdom. Favorite object: book, bookmark, or a chair no one else may use.
variants: Child-shaped spirit librarian with no romance role.
Clearly adult miniature scholar who insists on academic titles.

archetypes.title: Deadpan superior maid
archetypes.core: Perfect service accompanied by a perfectly timed insult.
archetypes.look: Design recipe: short pink, silver, ash, or black hair; compact or elegant adult build. Crisp monochrome uniform, apron, headpiece, sensible shoes, and an immaculate tray. Keep the silhouette simple enough that a glance or raised eyebrow supplies the comedy.
archetypes.engine: Dry, observant, and selective with loyalty. Wants order and standards. She follows a foolish instruction exactly enough to expose its foolishness, while behaving as though her comment was merely part of professional service.
archetypes.kit: Household management, intelligence gathering, or a narrowly chosen combat technique. Her employer's authority and obligations create limits. Signature object: tray, dusting cloth, or household ledger.
variants: Acerbic adult housekeeper with immaculate posture.
Formal male valet with understated sarcasm.

anchors.connection: Ram is an oni maid whose dry manner contrasts with her sister. She anchors the attendant's comic voice; flawless housekeeping is an original variation.

archetypes.title: Devoted combat maid
archetypes.core: A reassuring domestic uniform conceals an alarming capacity for violence.
archetypes.look: Design recipe: blue, black, or white hair; neat bob, braid, or pinned style, adult athletic or compact build. Apron and long skirt adapted for movement, hidden armor, and a weapon that is comically incompatible with housekeeping. Mechanical joints are an optional genre overlay.
archetypes.engine: Polite, diligent, and intensely protective. Wants to be useful without being discarded. She interprets hospitality as perimeter defense and cleans up before anyone has finished reacting to the fight.
archetypes.kit: Close defense, concealed weapons, and domestic competence. Give loyalty a boundary and her own preference. Signature object: cleaning tool that shares visual language with a weapon; android version adds maintenance needs.

Magic automaton maid who takes household requests literally.

archetypes.engine: Honorable, earnest, and proud of endurance. Wants to embody an ideal. In the comic branch, the ideal becomes absurd: she volunteers for every punishment, cannot hit anything, or rehearses speeches while the fight has already ended.
archetypes.kit: Defense, intimidation, and protection. Choose one weakness rather than copying every trait from a named character. Signature object: shield, dented helmet, or handbook of chivalry she keeps correcting.

Capable knight who is hopeless at ordinary conversation.

Adult adventurer whose aggressive manners conceal shy affection.

archetypes.engine: Courteous, idealistic, and more politically aware than the hero expects. Wants to protect her people and choose her own future. She makes a sincere personal request that casually creates a month of diplomatic work.

Royal candidate who needs allies but refuses to be treated as a prize.

archetypes.title: Merchant-minded noble partner
archetypes.core: A polished social ally who sees the business model behind every miracle.

Practical clothes with a small shared memento, training staff, or school item retained after transport. Her visual simplicity contrasts with royal and supernatural companions.

archetypes.title: Cursed outsider learning confidence

archetypes.look: Design recipe: adult slim, average, or sturdy build; pale blonde, lavender, or dark hair, partially concealed ears or marked hands. Layered travel clothes, protective gloves, a charm, and an object she is learning to touch or use safely.

archetypes.title: Hypercompetent sinister officer

archetypes.title: Boastful rival summoned hero

archetypes.title: Town guard captain

archetypes.title: Grateful farmer or craftsperson

archetypes.title: Slave trader or coercive contract broker
archetypes.core: Polished broker exposes a world's coercive institutions through contracts that treat vulnerable people as commercial assets.
archetypes.look: Combed dark hair, bald crown, or narrow mustache; controlled adult posture of any build. Expensive restrained coat, gloves, ledger, keys, stamped contracts, and a showroom-like office.
archetypes.engine: Uses courteous commercial language to normalize cruelty, insisting the paperwork makes everything reasonable. Parody can expose evasions and institutional hypocrisy without reducing captive characters to desirable merchandise.
archetypes.kit: Connects the plot to exploitation, debt, and unequal power. Track broker, captive, rescuer, employer, and companion as separate roles; escape or release does not manufacture romantic obligation.

archetypes.title: Demon lord final boss
archetypes.core: Remote enemy sovereign concentrates the quest's promised danger, theatrical reputation, and the question of ultimate purpose.

archetypes.title: Flamboyant demon general
archetypes.core: Memorable lieutenant turns a major encounter into personal theater through one obsessive theme and unmistakable silhouette.
archetypes.look: Crimson, white, or violet hair, elaborate mask, or distinctive horn arrangement; towering, skeletal, or elegantly narrow adult form. Dramatic collar, asymmetrical cape, signature weapon, and coordinated subordinate costumes.

archetypes.title: Misunderstood monster chief
archetypes.core: Feared nonhuman leader turns out to be negotiating food, security, and peaceful survival for their community.
archetypes.look: Heavy horns, tusks, fur, scales, or imposing ears; large or broad adult silhouette. Tribal mantle, practical armor, ceremonial staff, settlement tokens, and expressive eyes that soften the threatening outline.
archetypes.engine: Visitors expect a battle speech and receive a discussion of crop damage. Politeness can be awkward across cultures; strength protects the community rather than proving an automatic desire for conquest.

archetypes.title: Jobbing bureaucrat or accountant

harem_adventure.sustain_plan: Potions, rest, and access to a town healer; retreat remains possible.

generation_config.mechanism_rule: The primary protagonist establishes the one premise mechanism. Native elves, vampires, dragons, and slimes are not extra mechanisms. A newly introduced separate modern machine, time loop, mecha system, or second reincarnation gimmick needs an explicit compatibility override.
generation_config.rules_are: Editorial defaults except identity, relationship, declared mechanical dependencies, and consistency checks. Numeric weights and caps are design choices, not measured genre frequencies.
generation_config.role_promotion: A world NPC can become a party regular only when the instance explicitly changes narrative_role and supplies an ongoing contribution. An object keeps its role independent of body form.

rules: Being female, rescued, loyal, or nonhuman never creates a romance relationship automatically.
Present age and presentation are separate from past-life age and chronological age.
A child ward, child-form companion, animal familiar, or object does not receive a romantic slot by default.
A spirit may be contracted to a supporting character rather than to the protagonist.
NPC means narrative function in this catalog; it is not a claim that a local person is an in-world nonplayer character.
A relationship needs reciprocal goals or friction; mere admiration supplies little scene material.

visual_dimensions.recognition_rule: Choose a silhouette, a role prop, and a behavioral contradiction. Color is a supporting cue. Small party members should differ on at least three selected visual or behavioral dimensions; this is an editorial guideline, not a proven recognition threshold.

examples.title: The Totally Ordinary Survey Team

roster.label: The Loudest Nose in the Woods

examples.why: Five adults fill different conversational jobs: understatement, superiority, enthusiasm, concern, and friendly teasing. The elf supplies patient precision; the wolf supplies close pursuit. One elf and one beast-person create immediate visual separation without making ancestry determine personality. The receptionist remains a town contact.
examples.scene: The guild requests a sketch of a dangerous boulder. The hero gently taps it into gravel. The elf measures the remaining dust, the wolf celebrates, and the medic asks whether geological damage is covered by their deposit.
examples.limitations: The hero has overwhelming output but poor calibration. Companions retain navigation, medical, and social expertise. Recovery depends on supplies and returning to town; nobody gets every useful ability.

examples.title: Four Heroes and One Unpaid Invoice
examples.why: The rabbit can win the fight, the fairy can repair injuries, and the housekeeper can organize camp. Their leader's shortcuts turn those real strengths into financial disasters. The paid housekeeper travels by choice, while the fairy insists on itemized fees. Romance is off.
examples.scene: The leader negotiates a reward per defeated goblin. The rabbit captures them alive. The housekeeper charges for feeding the prisoners, and the fairy bills the leader for the headache he asked her to cure.
examples.limitations: Competence stays real; poor coordination causes the comedy. They cannot fight indefinitely without food and recovery funds. An M09 lead can replace M02, making expensive overpreparation the source of debt instead.

examples.title: The Broken Banner Escort
examples.why: Trust develops through agreed responsibilities: the defender holds ground, the swordswoman chooses openings, the guardian keeps escape routes clear, and the fairy tracks medical reserves. Everyone joins voluntarily. Two distinct animal-derived silhouettes coexist; neither is a pet or a purchased reward.
examples.scene: A merchant asks which companion belongs to the shield bearer. He points to the shield. The swordswoman points to her contract. The fairy points to the unpaid emergency-treatment clause, and all four suddenly agree on the importance of independence.
examples.limitations: Blocking damage does not finish encounters. Broken formations, exhausted supplies, and suspicion remain serious obstacles. Their bond progresses through kept promises rather than instant devotion, and romance stays off.

examples.title: The Armed Caravan and Its Competing Agendas
examples.why: All five are visibly adult original characters with independent aims: diplomacy, deliveries, professional respect, and trade. The princess courts the crafter through grand gestures; the courier invites him on competitive dates. The maid remains a paid nonromantic colleague, while the countess tests whether a business partnership could become personal. One elf and varied clothing keep the cast distinct.
examples.scene: The gunsmith unveils a practical new launcher. The princess requests floral engraving. The courier asks whether it can fire parcels. The countess presents the licensing contract before the maid finishes asking about cleaning instructions.
examples.limitations: Weapons need materials, maintenance, and judgment. The two declared romantic interests have different expectations; the professional and commercial relationships remain separate. Each companion has a reason to disagree or leave, so the hero cannot settle the cast's conflicts by building a larger gun.

examples.title: The Traveling Supper Club
examples.why: The cook supplies meals and planning; the wolf handles dangerous encounters; the slime handles small practical jobs. Their different sizes make a clear comic silhouette. A familiar-centered premise accommodates two creature companions without needing extra human romance leads. A trader supplies ingredients between journeys.
examples.scene: A village prepares a diplomatic banquet for the terrifying wolf. The cook quietly replaces it with stew. The wolf declares the village under his protection. The slime eats the written treaty, assuming it was the final course.
examples.limitations: The wolf's strength cannot obtain every ingredient or make the cook enjoy danger. The slime has a limited task list and needs guidance. Stock, cooking time, and the next safe campsite still matter.

examples.title: The Lecture Blade and the Quiet Stray

roster.label: The Quiet Stray
roster.role: clearly child catfolk ward and wielder

examples.why: This is a guardian-and-apprentice relationship with romance off. The sword supplies advice, borrowed magic, and its own telekinetic movement; the child chooses goals, observes local life, and willingly wields it. Their private telepathic channel is a defined rule. A trusted innkeeper supplies a home between short expeditions.
examples.scene: The sword rehearses a magnificent speech for negotiating a bridge toll. The child listens carefully, then offers to retrieve the keeper's stranded kitten. They cross for free. The sword spends the next mile explaining that kindness was also part of its strategy.
examples.limitations: Levitation does not give the blade a human social identity or authority over the child's choices. Training, food, rest, and adult community support remain necessary. The ward is not an adult simply because she fights well.

examples.title: The Shop That Needs a Lift
examples.why: The machine supplies products and constrained problem-solving; the carrier chooses routes and handles public conversation. Their friendship also operates as a practical business partnership. A recurring merchant is a supplier and customer, outside the core duo. No extra shapeshifter is needed to explain the premise.
examples.scene: The merchant asks whether the dispenser accepts credit. It announces, 'Please insert payment.' The carrier translates this into an elaborate speech about sacred commercial honor. The machine dispenses a receipt, and the merchant solemnly bows to it.
examples.limitations: The machine uses a fixed phrase bank, limited inventory, and a defined energy budget. Its carrier has her own goals and can refuse a route. The merchant cannot conjure nonexistent goods or unrestricted funds.

examples.title: The Villainess Garden Committee

roster.label: The Principled Neighbor Princess
roster.role: adult female political rival and ally

examples.why: All four are adult original court characters. Their shared human anatomy is deliberate: gardening tools, formal uniform, armor, and a diplomatic folio separate their roles. The princess competes over policy while remaining kind. Reputation, invitations, money, and public trust determine success more often than healing or damage.
examples.scene: The heroine invites her rival to prune roses, hoping to avoid a dangerous ball. The princess turns it into a charity event. The prince offers sponsorship. The knight discovers that the fundraiser now includes a dance.
examples.limitations: The heroine's remembered plot is incomplete, and other people have independent aims. Charm cannot erase conflicting duties. Court access and reliable allies matter; romance may involve eligible adults without making every friendship romantic.

examples.title: The Smallest Publisher in the Capital
examples.why: The child supplies an obsessive publishing goal, the patron obtains materials and customers, the dwarf develops workable tools, and the adult tutor checks methods. Child status and adult past-life memory stay separate. Production relationships, education, and care replace a harem structure. An outside noble can provide introductions.
examples.scene: The bookmaker announces a cheap book for every household. The patron shows the paper bill. The dwarf proudly unveils a press too large for the doorway. The professor assigns everyone a lesson on measuring before inventing.
examples.limitations: Knowledge does not supply strength, money, literacy, or manufacturing capacity. The child requires rest and protection; adults retain expertise and decision-making. Progress follows a credible chain of small experiments.

world_contacts.label: The Kindly Seal Holder
world_contacts.role: noble sponsor outside the workplace core

examples.title: The Undead Office of Public Comfort
examples.why: This is a governing organization. Two undead and two demons are deliberate exceptions: exposed skeletal robes contrast with sealed armor, while the formal strategist contrasts with the casual heiress. The ruler sets policy, officers interpret it, and residents judge the results. Romance is off.
examples.scene: The ruler requests a shorter queue at the permit office. The strategist redraws the district so the queue is technically elsewhere. The heiress opens a second window. The armor steward respectfully records her solution as a revolutionary doctrine.
examples.limitations: Force cannot manufacture public confidence, competent services, or honest feedback. Retainers have domains and information limits. Similar species require different silhouettes and responsibilities, not interchangeable fanatical devotion.

examples.title: The Cottage With Too Many Chore Specialists
examples.why: One household unifies the supernatural cast. The witch seeks rest, the dragon takes pride in useful work, the elf runs a legitimate craft business, and the ghost wants belonging. Different powers create different domestic complications. Only one elf appears, and household relationships remain nonromantic.
examples.scene: The witch asks everyone to dry the laundry. The dragon scorches one sleeve. The pharmacist offers a restorative mixture that turns everything green. The ghost, who cannot wear the clothes, is appointed quality inspector.
examples.limitations: Great power cannot replace apologies, customer refunds, or careful housekeeping. The ghost's physical interactions need consistent rules. Visiting neighbors provide variety without permanently adding another dragon, elf, or mascot to every scene.

examples.title: The Promotion Nobody Requested
examples.why: P28 deliberately uses a human military variant; sinister efficiency does not imply a demon in this setting. The child commander brings adult bureaucratic thinking, the major converts it into plans, and the sergeant connects orders to daily soldiering. Native troops, supply staff, and medical personnel exist outside the focal trio.
examples.scene: The commander requests a quiet desk assignment. The major concludes that headquarters needs a desk closer to the front. The sergeant proudly packs a portable one. New orders announce a promotion and a parachute.
examples.limitations: This is a military ensemble, not a guild party. Command authority, logistics, injury, and uncertainty constrain magic. The commander remains visibly a child, relationships are professional, and romance is off.
